fields.why: The Summary's headline is 2016 brand shares and the 2015 ad-exposure contrast, not a change over time; the trend analyses are secondary, so the repeated-cross-section trend rule (headline is a change) does not add before/after or trend.

Race p-values attach to highest-vs-lowest claims under a blanket 'chi-squared tests ... subgroup differences' line, which the brief's blanket-test clause reads as per-group vs referent; an r x c chi-square across the 3 race groups (omnibus) is also defensible since the test's layout is not stated.
The trend model adjusts for grade (an age proxy), so age is also a covariate; A recorded race and sex as covariates from the same clause but missed grade.

The regression's contrast is the 2012-2016 trend; its unadjusted counterpart is only 2012 and 2016 percentages set side by side, with no crude trend test or ratio. A's evidence (chi-square for subgroup differences) concerns other contrasts.

brief_issues: The blanket-test clause for per-group vs referent cites t-tests; it does not say whether a blanket chi-square statement under highest/lowest claims across 3+ SPD groups is per-group or an omnibus test under groupwise rule 2.
